model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) in percentage (%) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from $10^0$ to $10^4$, with major tick marks at $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is a linear scale from 40 to 65, with major tick marks at intervals of 5. The "Base" method (black line with circles) shows a steady increase from approximately 39% to 44%. The "MEND" method (brown line with diamonds) increases from about 44% to 56%. The "FT" method (blue line with triangles) rises from 40% to 48%. The "MEMIT" method (purple line with squares) increases from 43% to 55%. The "ROME" method (green line with squares) shows the highest accuracy, increasing from 51% to 66%. All methods exhibit a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
